outlier detection and trend detection are two sides of the same coin.
(i) outlier detection methods are useful for trend detection and that (ii) trend detection methods are useful in outlier detection.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the question whether there are any similarities between outlier detection and trend detection.
two questions: 1) How do outlier detection and trend detection relate to each other?
the question: What can outlier detection learn from trend detection, and vice versa?
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the two tasks are indeed very different, but that they are related and can be approached in the same way.
outlier detection is the process of detecting unexpected observations in a data set and trend detection is the process to find a sudden change in the distribution of data over time.
trend detection is a more general problem than outlier detection and that the latter can be seen as a special case of the former.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found that many outlier detection methods are also useful for trend detection and vice versa.
we are able to detect outliers in high-dimensional data by using a trend detection algorithm.
we have developed the first outlier and trend detection algorithms that can work on the same data stream and that can even be used together in a single system to detect both types of events.
The main takeaway from our work is that
outlier detection and trend detection should be seen as two sides of the same coin, and that the same methods can be used for both.
trend detection is not a separate problem from outlier detection.

trend detection is essentially an outlier detection problem in a data stream, with the difference that the data stream is not just a sequence of vectors in Euclid-ean space, but a sequence of sets of such vectors, and that the goal is not to find the rarest object, but to find the most frequent one.
